title: Sapphire Systems - Private VPC Discovery

Agreed next steps include sharing deployment checklist, network diagram template, pricing ranges for reserved capacity, and scheduling a technical deep-dive and benchmark run in their staging VPC.

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-01-18T15:00:00-07:00 | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Sapphire), Alex Gomez (Cloud Architect), Maya Lin (Security Lead)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): discussion around private VPC deploy, network topology, KMS, logs, SSO, timeline.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Lena from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on your account. Marco from our SE team is here too, we'll mainly listen for requirements and then sketch out next steps.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Thanks Len a quick intro, i'm Priya, CTO at Sapphire Systems. We're looking at moving some of our LLM workloads off public hosted endpoints into a private VPC deployment, mostly for compliance and data residency.
[00:25] Marco Diaz: Hi all, Marco. quick question up front — is this a replacement for your existing inference cluster or is it new workload?
[00:30] Alex Gomez: it's mostly new, we're piloting in staging and if that goes well we'll migrate a couple of services. We do have internal GPU infra but it's not tuned for high token throughput, so we're evaluating Redwood for both performance and ops.
[00:45] Maya Lin: our security asks are standard: SOC2, audit logs delivered into our S3, KMS integration (prefer customer-managed keys), and SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning ideally.
[00:58] Lena Park: perfect, that's in-line with other customers. On the networking side do you want a fully private endpoint (no internet egress) or are you okay with egress through a NAT/bastion?
[01:10] Alex Gomez: preference is fully private; we want traffic to stay within our VPCs. How does Redwood set up private connectivity?
[01:18] Marco Diaz: we support a few patterns: VPC peering for single-region small setups, Transit Gateway for multi-VPC multi-region topologies, or private interface endpoints if you prefer us to publish endpoints into your account. For AWS specifically we can set up customer-controlled interface endpoints and route traffic directly to our worker pools, or we can request peering if CIDR ranges don't overlap.
[01:45] Priya Nair: what about cross-region? we need EU data residency for EU customers and US for NA. can we pin region per workload?
[01:54] Marco Diaz: yes, you can pin model routing by region. Redwood's control plane can be in our control plane region, but compute can be deployed in your chosen regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1, etc. we do recommend deploying workers in the region where the data resides to avoid cross-border transit.
[02:12] Alex Gomez: ok, sounds good. A couple network specifics: our VPC is 10.0.0.0/16 in us-west-2 and 10.1.0.0/16 in eu-west-1, we also have a TGW. any CIDR overlap concerns?
[02:22] Marco Diaz: that CIDR plan is clean — no overlap — so peering or TGW will work. if there were overlaps we could route via a Transit Gateway with NATing or run a proxy in a neutral VPC, but that's more involved.
[02:36] Maya Lin: about audit logs — can Redwood push logs directly into our S3 bucket in our account, or do we have to pull them from Redwood?
[02:44] Lena Park: we can deliver audit logs and usage logs into your account via cross-account S3 delivery. typical pattern is a dedicated bucket plus an IAM role we write to, or you can pull via our secure delivery API. We'll share the runbook for log delivery.
[02:59] Priya Nair: KMS — we need to use our CMKs, HSM backed if possible. how does key management work?
[03:07] Marco Diaz: we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in KMS. For HSM-backed keys you'll need to provide the key ARN and we'll set up key policies and IAM role assumptions. For private deployments there's also an option to bring-your-own-HSM in some on-prem cases, but for VPC-hosted deployments CMKs in your AWS account are standard.
[03:28] Alex Gomez: any constraints around latency for the key calls? we've had issues where KMS latency adds to token generation latency in tight loops.
[03:36] Marco Diaz: good call — we cache encryption keys and use envelope encryption so the per-token path doesn't call KMS. only initial key unwraps or rotation touch KMS; runtime uses cached DEKs inside our worker where allowed by policy.
[03:50] Priya Nair: what's the typical network setup — do we need a public NAT gateway for model downloads or is that done via your side?
[03:58] Lena Park: model binaries are typically pulled into the worker pool during provisioning. For Private deployments we can either pull through an outbound egress in your VPC or host model artifacts in an S3 bucket in your account and we fetch from there. If you want zero egress we recommend pre-populating an S3 bucket in your account and giving our provisioning role access.
[04:18] Alex Gomez: and region constraints — if we want EU-only for certain projects, how do you enforce routing?
[04:24] Marco Diaz: we have policies in the control plane to pin workloads to specific clusters/regions. routing policies can be set per-api-key or per-tenant to ensure EU traffic never leaves eu-west-1. We'll show the config in the deep-dive.
[04:36] Maya Lin: on compliance, do you provide SOC2 Type II evidence and penetration test reports?
[04:41] Lena Park: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation docs we can share under an NDA. we'll also include our pen test summary in the compliance pack.
[04:52] Priya Nair: regarding SSO, we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. can Redwood integrate with our IdP and map roles to RBAC?
[04:59] Marco Diaz: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning and role mappings. We can map Okta groups to Redwood roles; we'll include the SAML metadata template in the checklist.
[05:12] Alex Gomez: two practicalities — ports, firewall rules, and DNS. do we need special DNS entries for private endpoints?
[05:20] Marco Diaz: for interface endpoints we publish a private DNS name into your VPC. For peering you route to our worker subnets. We'll provide example security group rules and required ports (mostly TLS 443, and a few ephemeral ports for management).
[05:36] Priya Nair: any latency numbers from similar customers? we care about 95th percentile latency under 200 ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens.
[05:44] Marco Diaz: typical 95p for that workload on Dedicated is sub-150ms in-region; Private depends on your network hops. We'll run a benchmark in your staging VPC to validate and tune batching and model variant selection.
[05:58] Lena Park: note on pricing — Dedicated/reserved capacity has a different pricing profile than hosted. we'll share a rough estimate now and a formal quote once we scope your expected QPS and token volumes.
[06:08] Alex Gomez: about provisioning timelines — how long to stand up a private cluster in our VPC?
[06:13] Marco Diaz: once network connectivity and IAM roles are settled, typical lead time is 2-3 weeks for a basic cluster. If you need HSM or on-prem connectors add extra time.
[06:25] Priya Nair: what's the fallback policy if capacity is constrained? we don't want outages.
[06:31] Lena Park: you can configure fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant or a smaller model in a separate failover region. we can set SLOs and alerting via the Redwood Console.
[06:44] Priya Nair: any gotchas with CIDR overlaps and our TGW?
[06:48] Marco Diaz: TGW is fine; just need route table entries and ensure no overlapping CIDRs. If overlap exists we recommend using an intermediary VPC or NAT translation.
[06:58] Alex Gomez: can we have audit logs show both usage and per-token cost breakdown?
[07:04] Lena Park: yes, our logs include token-level usage and route/model-level cost breakdowns. We'll show sample logs.
[07:12] Priya Nair: ok good. timeline-wise we want a pilot in staging in the next 3-4 weeks.
[07:18] Lena Park: that's realistic. next steps we'll send you the checklist, sample network diagram, pricing ranges, and availability for the benchmark.
[07:26] Marco Diaz: I'll own the benchmark and bring a short plan to the deep-dive — will need staging VPC access or an engineer to run agents inside your VPC.
[07:35] Alex Gomez: we'll probably run the agent ourselves with your instructions; easier from a security standpoint.
[07:40] Maya Lin: and we'll send our security requirements doc and expected retention periods for logs.
[07:46] Priya Nair: any other questions on your side?
[07:50] Lena Park: nothing else here. thanks for the clarity.
[07:53] Priya Nair: thanks.
